1931:  * number of elements removed from the stream. The 'approx' option, if non-zero,
1932:  * specifies that the trimming must be performed in a approximated way in
1933:  * order to maximize performances. This means that the stream may contain
1934:  * entries with IDs < 'id' in case of MINID (or more elements than 'maxlen'
1935:  * in case of MAXLEN), and elements are only removed if we can remove
1936:  * a *whole* node of the radix tree. The elements are removed from the head
1937:  * of the stream (older elements).
1938:  *
1939:  * The function may return zero if:
1940:  *
1941:  * 1) The minimal entry ID of the stream is already < 'id' (MINID); or
1942:  * 2) The stream is already shorter or equal to the specified max length (MAXLEN); or
1943:  * 3) The 'approx' option is true and the head node did not have enough elements
1944:  *    to be deleted.
1945:  *
1946:  * args->limit is the maximum number of entries to delete. The purpose is to
1947:  * prevent this function from taking to long.
1948:  * If 'limit' is 0 then we do not limit the number of deleted entries.
1949:  * Much like the 'approx', if 'limit' is smaller than the number of entries
1950:  * that should be trimmed, there is a chance we will still have entries with
1951:  * IDs < 'id' (or number of elements >= maxlen in case of MAXLEN).
1952:  *
1953:  * Implemented next to the radix-tree iterator so that node walking, key
1954:  * buffers and associated listpack payloads can be handled together.
1955:  */

1961:     int trim_strategy = args->trim_strategy;

1968:     raxSeek(&ri,"^",NULL,0);
1969: 
1970:     int64_t deleted = 0;
1971:     while (raxNext(&ri)) {
1972:         if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_MAXLEN && s->length <= maxlen)
1973:             break;
1974: 
1975:         unsigned char *lp = ri.data, *p = lpFirst(lp);
1976:         int64_t entries = lpGetInteger(p);
1977: 
1978:         /* Check if we exceeded the amount of work we could do */
1979:         if (limit && (deleted + entries) > limit)
1980:             break;
1981: 
1982:         /* Check if we can remove the whole node. */
1983:         int remove_node;
1984:         streamID master_id = {0}; /* For MINID */
1985:         if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_MAXLEN) {

243: /* Get an edge streamID of a given listpack.

247:    if (lp == NULL)

250:    unsigned char *lp_ele;

252:    /* We need to seek either the first or the last entry depending
253:     * on the direction of the iteration. */
254:    if (first) {
255:        /* Get the master fields count. */
256:        lp_ele = lpFirst(lp);        /* Seek items count */
257:        lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele); /* Seek deleted count. */
258:        lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele); /* Seek num fields. */
259:        int64_t master_fields_count = lpGetInteger(lp_ele);
260:        lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele); /* Seek first field. */
261: 
262:        /* If we are iterating in normal order, skip the master fields
263:         * to seek the first actual entry. */
264:        for (int64_t i = 0; i < master_fields_count; i++)
265:            lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele);

267:        /* If we are going forward, skip the previous entry's
268:         * lp-count field (or in case of the master entry, the zero
269:         * term field) */
270:        lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele);
271:        if (lp_ele == NULL)
272:            return 0;
273:    } else {
274:        /* If we are iterating in reverse direction, just seek the
275:         * last part of the last entry in the listpack (that is, the
276:         * fields count). */
277:        lp_ele = lpLast(lp);

279:        /* If we are going backward, read the number of elements this
